summary: CKGSB's global marketing team is in launch week for the CKGSB-IE China Going-Global report while finalizing the Intelligent China program page and the knowledge website redesign, with Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top marketing priorities.
summaryDetail: The immediate priority is the CKGSB-IE report launch on September 15: Ira, Xuan, and Julie must share the report webpage ahead of the launch, Felix needs to review the press release (now titled 'CKGSB-IE University Report Reveals New Models for Chinese Companies Going Global'), and the team must promote it on social media. In parallel, the Intelligent China program page copy requires sign-off from Cao Yi and Jay, and the Emerging Tech Management Week webpage rewrite by Manaferra needs review from Alan, Renee, and Xin. The knowledge website redesign is also active, with Joseph to share the HTML design file and a half-hour feedback meeting to be scheduled, while Joker implements changes based on feedback. This week also demands operational follow-through: finalizing alumni confirmations and approvals for the Tech in Asia luncheon (Melvin Lim to confirm Caroline Tang and Loh Yiwen and approve Zachary Zhou, Yvonne Song, and Yijia Wang), sharing the August 2026 CKGSB Business Conditions Index with the network, and resolving lingering Outlook login issues across devices. Looking ahead, the team must continue prioritizing Asia Star and Intelligent China for SEO and marketing, analyze existing participant profiles, and get a brief on conversion tracking setup, all while keeping US partnerships on hold for the first quarter.

meetings.title: Knowledge Website Design Review
meetings.summary: The team reviewed the proposed knowledge website design, noting it is similar to the current site with menu categorization as the main improvement. They discussed incorporating inspiration from Joseph's editorial-style layout to display more articles and indices, and agreed on next steps for refinement.

meetings.title: CKGSB Global Marketing Strategy Meeting
meetings.summary: The team discussed prioritizing China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for SEO and marketing, with US programs as secondary. They also reviewed conversion tracking setup and agreed on next steps for research and content optimization.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel and integrate videos into topics instead of having a separate category.
Keep the knowledge menu centered rather than left-aligned.
Incorporate BCI and BSI indices into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Use Joseph's design as inspiration, particularly for displaying more articles and indices, but not adopt it wholesale.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two marketing priorities, with Berkeley as a possible third.
Put US partnerships on hold for the first quarter to focus on China programs.
Approved attendees for Tech in Asia: Zachary Zhou, Yvonne Song, Yijia Wang, Loh Yiwen
